title: Lettersly
descriptor: A daily web-based riddle game where you spend to solve. Buy riddles and letter probes to work out what the answer is, and bank whatever budget survives.

items.title: Lettersly
items.body: One riddle a day, and one word that answers it. You start with a budget, and that budget is also your score — every riddle you unlock and every letter you probe is paid for out of the points you are trying to keep. Read it right early and you bank the rest. Guess wrong and the wallet empties.

title: AI Suitability Ticket Classifier
descriptor: Turns raw support ticket exports into a structured map of what customers actually ask for, what data an answer needs, and which of those requests an AI copilot can safely handle.

items.title: AI Suitability Ticket Classifier
items.body: Before you can automate support, you have to know what support is actually doing. This pipeline reads a ticket export, extracts every customer intent, works out what data an answer would require, and assigns each ticket an AI-suitability tier — then audits its own tier calls with a second, deterministic method.

nodes.title: Clean Export
nodes.body: Strips personal data and markup from the raw export before anything reaches a model

nodes.title: Classify Tickets
nodes.body: Two GPT-5.4 calls per ticket — an actionability gate, then a strict-schema extraction of intents, required data and a suitability tier

nodes.title: Cluster Intents
nodes.body: mxbai-embed-large embeddings, UMAP plus HDBSCAN, then GPT-5.4 writes the category labels

nodes.title: Normalize Data Needs
nodes.body: A GPT-5.4 pass collapses free-text data requirements into consistent groups, keeping the raw wording

nodes.title: Re-derive Tier
nodes.body: Deterministic rules first, with all-mpnet-base-v2 similarity as the fallback — no model verdict is taken on trust

nodes.title: audit agrees?
nodes.body: Divergence Route — an independent read-only pass flags disputed tiers instead of overwriting them

nodes.title: Aggregate + Report
nodes.body: Rolls topics and tier distribution into the executive report

outputs.title: Dataset + Report
outputs.caption: Per-ticket intents, data needs and tiers, plus the executive summary

outputs.title: Divergence Queue
outputs.caption: Tickets where the two methods disagree go to human review

items.title: GPT-5.4 family
items.body: gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4, picked per role so cheap calls do the cheap work. Reasoning effort is tuned per stage rather than left at one setting.

items.title: Claude, switchable
items.body: claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-6 sit behind a one-line provider swap, which is also how batch mode gets used to roughly halve spend.

items.title: mxbai-embed-large
items.body: Runs locally through Ollama to embed every extracted intent, so the clustering pass costs nothing per run and never leaves the machine.

items.title: all-mpnet-base-v2
items.body: Backs the independent tier audit: when regex bucketing cannot place a ticket, sentence similarity decides, under an explicit floor and margin.

items.title: UMAP + HDBSCAN
items.body: Not models but the shape of the taxonomy — dimensional reduction then density clustering, with unstable cluster IDs canonicalised across runs.

items.title: qwen3:14b
items.body: A local model kept available for offline labelling experiments, so prompt changes can be tried without spending on a hosted call.

items.title: Never trust the model's own verdict
items.body: The suitability tier is recomputed from three yes/no facts the model must state, then re-derived a second time by a deterministic pass that flags disagreement rather than silently correcting it.

items.title: Brand-agnostic by composition
items.body: One universal rules block plus a per-brand examples file. Adding a brand is a prompt folder, not a code branch — and a linter enforces the shared wording rules after generation.

items.title: Cost and failure economics
items.body: Batch mode roughly halves spend, reasoning effort is tuned per role, and retries resend only unresolved tickets under a hard attempt cap with a bounded tolerance for stragglers.

items.title: A silent failure, encoded as guardrails
items.body: One run collapsed nearly two hundred labels into near-duplicates and reported zero cost. The fix — batched schema-bound mapping, per-item completeness checks and an explicit taxonomy status — is now permanent.

items.title: Stable IDs over unstable clusters
items.body: Density clustering renumbers itself on every rerun, so cluster identity is canonicalised per category and subcategory pair to keep comparisons across runs meaningful.

items.title: Known gap, stated plainly
items.body: Chunks are buffered in memory and written once, so a mid-run kill loses classifications already paid for. Runtime checkpointing is the next change, not a claimed feature.

title: Closed-Loop LLM Evals
descriptor: The classifier's existing checks validate one guess against another guess. This closes the loop against what actually happened to the ticket, and writes the correction itself.

items.title: Closed-Loop Evals
items.body: The classifier can tell you a ticket was safe for an AI copilot. Nothing in it could tell you whether that call survived contact with the customer. This system scores the highest-confidence tier against real ticket outcomes — replies, reopens, resolution — and when the tier stops holding up, it writes its own correction and commits it.

nodes.title: Select Predictions
nodes.body: Narrows to the tickets the classifier called safe for a copilot to answer

nodes.title: Pull Outcomes
nodes.body: Fetches replies, reopens, channel and status in batches, only for tickets settled long enough to judge

nodes.title: Score Hold-Up
nodes.body: Joins prediction to outcome per subcategory and computes how often the tier actually held

nodes.title: enough evidence?
nodes.body: Correction Gate — a thin sample or a healthy rate leaves the pipeline here

nodes.title: Write Correction
nodes.body: Caps the tier for that subcategory and has GPT-5.4 draft the counter-example appended to the brand's prompt

nodes.title: Feed Next Run
nodes.body: The next classification run reads the cap and the new example — no human step in the loop

outputs.title: Correction + Commit
outputs.caption: Override, prompt example and a commit carrying the stats that triggered it

outputs.title: Trend Logged Only
outputs.caption: Below the sample floor, or holding up fine — recorded, nothing changed

items.title: No model scores the outcome
items.body: Whether a tier held up is computed from reply counts, reopens and channel. Deliberately arithmetic, because a model judging its own earlier call is what this system exists to replace.

items.title: GPT-5.4 drafts the correction
items.body: The only generative step: once the numbers trip the gate, it writes the negative example appended to that brand's prompt file.

items.title: Same provider swap
items.body: It shares the classifier's client, so the Claude configuration — claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5 — applies here without separate wiring.

items.title: The cap is not generated
items.body: The tier ceiling itself is written as plain configuration, not model output, so every automated change stays reviewable and revertible in version control.

blocks.title: Automating a change to your own prompts

items.title: Ground truth, not a second opinion
items.body: Held up means the customer did not reopen and did not need to keep replying. Chat channels are excluded from the rate rather than counted against it, because a chat reply means something different.

items.title: A lag gate before judging
items.body: Only tickets closed long enough to have reopened are pulled. Score too early and every not-yet-reopened ticket flatters the tier.

items.title: Version control as the review step
items.body: There is no human approval gate. A minimum sample floor decides whether to act, every correction commits with the statistics that caused it, and revert is the rollback path.

items.title: Minimal blast radius
items.body: Exactly one functional change to the existing classifier — a tier cap it reads on the way out. Everything else is additive files and prompt text.

items.title: Scope held deliberately narrow
items.body: Only the top tier is validated. The middle tiers need drafted-versus-sent reply comparison, which is a different problem and is explicitly deferred.

items.title: Unknowns kept visible
items.body: The sample floor and hold-up threshold are provisional pending calibration, and any data-quality quirk in the platform counts as truth until it is coded around.
